title: Changelog Generator Architecture Draft (library vs service) — v0.3
content:
Owner: Michael Nguyen (Control Plane)
Last edited: 2025-10-14
Doc status: draft / working notes. Expect churn.

---

1) TL;DR
We need a deterministic way to generate customer-visible model release notes + internal change history from structured events and model metadata (schema v1). Key decisions:
- Do we ship the generator as a library called by other services (control plane / registry / docs build), or as a standalone “changelog-generator” service with storage + APIs?
- What is the contract between event producers (control plane/model registry) and release note consumers (Console, docs-site build, Support/audit tooling)?
- How do we handle backfill and idempotency so we don’t re-publish (or lose) notes?

Current leaning (as of 10/14): Hybrid.
- A shared “generator core” library (templating + mapping + redaction) used in:
  (a) a small internal service for ingestion + persistence + query APIs (Console needs pagination/filtering)
  (b) CI “preview” job that renders the exact same templates for PR review.

---

2) Problem statement / constraints recap
Today, model/version changes are recorded in multiple places (registry data, runtime configs, PRs, docs notes). This causes:
- silent promotions (customer sees different behavior but no notes)
- inconsistent wording and missing rollback guidance
- Support can’t quickly answer “what changed for this model, for this account, on this date?”
- Private deployments need exportable notes aligned to upgrade bundles

Hard constraints:
- Must not leak internal-only details in customer-visible notes (public vs internal field strategy).
- Notes must be reproducible and attributable (event->note traceability).
- Works across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; availability timing can differ.
- Handles A/B and canary rollouts without spamming confusing notes.

---

3) Terminology (working)
- Model: logical product name customers select (e.g., “rw-llama-3.1-70b”).
- Version: semantic version for a served artifact (e.g., 3.1.2). Includes tokenizer/runtime constraints + eval pointers.
- Variant: compat/behavior-affecting variant (e.g., “instruct”, “base”, “vision”).
- Profile: quantization / runtime profile (e.g., fp16, int8, gptq-4bit) — can be a separate “served artifact” under same model.
- Change event: structured record emitted on metadata update / promotion / deprecation.
- Release note entry: generated human-readable text with category/severity, plus links + guidance.

---

4) Inputs / outputs

4.1 Inputs (sources of truth)
Primary input should be structured events from the control plane and/or model registry (see ADR-0143). For MVP:
- model.metadata_changed
- model.version_promoted
- model.version_deprecated
- model.rollout_phase_changed (optional for v1; may be needed for “release notes during rollout” UX)

Event payload must carry:
- event_id (globally unique)
- occurred_at
- actor (service + human if applicable)
- scope (deployment=Hosted/Dedicated/Private, region, account_id? [see below])
- model identifier(s)
- schema_version + metadata_schema_hash
- diff summary (preferred) OR before/after pointers so generator can compute diff

Important: We should not rely on Git tags / PR labels as primary source, but we can use PR labeling as an *annotation* step for better wording.

4.2 Outputs (consumers)
- Console: per-model change history + global release notes feed (filter by deployment/region), RBAC-aware.
- Docs: public release notes pages + feeds (RSS/JSON). Must be deterministic and stable under rebuilds.
- Support/audit: internal-only view + audit event correlation, export for escalations.
- Private packaging: bundle export for offline, tied to upgrade artifact.

---

5) Key design principles
1) Deterministic rendering
Given the same event + metadata snapshot, we should always produce the same output.

2) One rendering pipeline
Avoid “docs has one template, Console has another” drift. Use shared templates (or template library + versioning).

3) Public/internal separation as a first-class invariant
Do not trust downstream consumers to hide internal fields. Generator should produce explicitly separated outputs (public vs internal) and sign them (or at least stamp provenance fields).

4) Idempotency and replay-safe
Events will be retried. We must handle at-least-once delivery.

5) Editorial control without free-form chaos
We want consistency, but we need a mechanism for humans to provide “release note hint” fields (short change summary, customer impact) without turning into hand-written notes.

---

6) Architecture options

Option A: Library only (no dedicated service)
- Generator packaged as a library used by:
  - control plane during promotion
  - docs build pipeline (pull metadata + generate)
  - Console backend (generate on the fly)

Pros:
- Fewer moving parts (no new service).
- No additional storage to operate.

Cons:
- “Generate on the fly” is risky: changes to templates could rewrite historical notes.
- Console needs pagination + filtering across many events; recomputing diff/render for each request is expensive and inconsistent.
- Hard to support “what did customer X see on date Y?” without persisted output.
- Harder to enforce strict public/internal separation across multiple call sites.

Conclusion: Not recommended for anything beyond CI preview.

Option B: Standalone service (ingest events -> persist rendered entries -> serve APIs)
Components:
- Event consumer (Kafka/PubSub/SQS — TBD; currently we have internal event bus)
- Storage (Postgres recommended for query + indexing; optionally blob storage for full artifacts)
- Template renderer + redaction engine
- Query APIs for Console/docs/admin

Pros:
- Stable, immutable record of what we published.
- Natural place to enforce redaction + RBAC.
- Easier backfill via batch ingestion.
- Observability and replay controls in one place.

Cons:
- New service to deploy + operate (SLOs, paging).
- Need to define clear contract between event producers and generator.

Conclusion: Recommended for MVP if Console is in-scope (it is).

Option C: Hybrid (service + shared core library)
- “core” package: diffing, category mapping, template rendering, redaction rules, output schema
- service uses core for ingestion; CI preview uses core for PR checks

Pros:
- Single rendering logic across service + CI.
- Still get persistence + query.

Cons:
- Slightly more packaging discipline (versioning core).

Conclusion: Best overall.

---

7) Proposed MVP: Hybrid

7.1 High-level flow
1) Control plane emits model metadata change events on:
   - edit (metadata_changed)
   - promotion (version_promoted)
   - deprecation (version_deprecated)
2) changelog-generator service consumes events
3) Service resolves metadata snapshot(s) (from registry/control plane API) OR uses embedded payloads
4) Service computes a structured “note model” (category, severity, impacted surfaces)
5) Service renders:
   - public entry (customer safe)
   - internal entry (includes extra diagnostics and internal rationale)
6) Service persists rendered entries (immutable)
7) Console reads entries via API (RBAC aware)
8) Docs build reads “public entries” via API OR via artifact export

Note: we should treat “rendered entry” as immutable; template changes should apply only to new entries (or via explicit backfill job that creates a new entry version).

7.2 Storage model (working)
We likely need:
- entries table keyed by entry_id (stable) + event_id (unique)
- index fields: model_id, model_version, deployment_mode, region, created_at
- visibility: public/internal
- entry_version: integer (so we can supersede)
- supersedes_entry_id: optional

Also store provenance:
- template_bundle_version
- generator_core_version
- metadata_schema_hash

---

8) Templating approach

8.1 Requirements
- Consistent taxonomy (security/breaking/perf/quality/bugfix/deprecation)
- Severity language per style guide
- Links to guidance (rollbacks, pinning, compatibility)
- Avoid overclaiming quality changes; require statistical significance gate before “improved quality” language

8.2 Template strategy
- Use a small set of templates keyed by:
  - event_type (promoted vs metadata update vs deprecation)
  - change_category (breaking/security/perf/quality/etc)
  - model_family optional (some models have known special notes)

- Keep templates mostly parameterized with a constrained input object:
  - “impact_summary” (short)
  - “what_changed” bullet list derived from diff categories
  - “customer_action” guidance (pin/rollback/no action)
  - “availability” block (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

- Allow one optional free-form field from metadata (“release_notes_hint”) but:
  - length limit
  - no URLs except allowlist
  - must pass redaction checks
  - must be explicitly tagged as public or internal

8.3 Suggested template representation
We can store templates as versioned files in repo (generator core), e.g.
- templates/v1/version_promoted_breaking.md
- templates/v1/version_promoted_nonbreaking.md
- templates/v1/deprecated.md

Rendering engine can be Mustache/Handlebars-like with very limited logic (avoid complex branching).

8.4 Redaction and “public/internal” separation
Strong preference: generator renders two completely separate artifacts.
- public_artifact: safe for docs and Console non-admin roles
- internal_artifact: includes internal rationale, linked incident tickets, internal-only perf numbers, etc.

Rules:
- Any field not explicitly tagged public defaults to internal.
- If an event includes “internal_only_reason”, it must never be present in public output.
- PII and customer identifiers must never be included in public output.
- For Dedicated/Private: account-specific notes should be internal unless explicitly allowed.

Open question: do we ever show account-scoped release notes to the account? (Probably later; out of scope per PRD.)

---

9) Backfill strategy

We need a small backfill so customers immediately see something in change history when this launches.

9.1 Backfill goals
- Not full historical rewrite.
- Enough to cover:
  - last N promotions per top models
  - any currently active deprecations
  - any security-relevant changes in last 60 days (if available)

9.2 Backfill sources
A) Replay events from event bus (preferred if retention exists)
- If event retention >= 30–90 days, we can consume from offset T.
- Needs idempotency (event_id uniqueness).

B) Snapshot diff backfill
- Pull latest model registry records pre/post migration (or tagged snapshots)
- Generate synthetic “backfill events” with occurred_at approximated
- Mark entries as backfilled = true and link to migration job id

C) “Manual seed file” for a few flagship models
- Worst case: curated seed entries for top 10 models to avoid empty UI
- Should be avoided if we can backfill via A/B

Recommendation:
- Do A for whatever window is available.
- Do B for missing gaps (esp. for Private bundles where event replay may not exist).
- Clearly label backfilled entries in internal output; public output should not call attention to backfill unless needed.

9.3 Idempotency details
- All ingested events must have stable event_id.
- On ingest: UPSERT on event_id; if already present, skip.
- If we need to “correct” a note: emit a new event type (e.g., note_corrected) or support superseding entry with a new entry_version.

---

10) API contract sketches (internal)

Non-goal: perfect API design here. This is to unblock Console + docs integration conversations.

10.1 Console query APIs
GET /internal/changelog/v1/models/{model_id}/history?visibility=public|internal&deployment_mode=hosted|dedicated|private&region=us-east-1&limit=50&cursor=...
Response: list of rendered entries + minimal structured metadata.

GET /internal/changelog/v1/release-notes/feed?visibility=public|internal&deployment_mode=...&since=2025-10-01T00:00:00Z&limit=50&cursor=...
Use: Console “Recent model changes” feed.

10.2 Docs consumption
Two possible patterns:
A) Docs build pulls from API
GET /public/changelog/v1/release-notes?model_id=...&limit=... (public-only)
Pros: simple, no artifact copying
Cons: docs build now depends on service availability

B) Artifact export job (preferred)
- Service writes daily/hourly JSON artifacts to blob storage
- Docs build reads artifact by date/version
Example artifact name:
- s3://redwood-changelog-artifacts/public/2025-10-14/release-notes.jsonl
Pros: docs builds are reproducible, decoupled
Cons: one more pipeline piece

Recommendation: do B for docs; keep API for Console.

10.3 Output schema (rendered entry)
We should define a stable “rendered entry” structure. Rough sketch:
- entry_id
- event_id
- occurred_at
- model_id
- model_version
- title
- category (breaking/security/perf/quality/bugfix/deprecation)
- severity (critical/high/medium/low)
- summary (1-2 sentences)
- details_markdown (bullets)
- customer_action (none/recommend_pin/recommend_review/recommend_migrate)
- links (docs URLs)
- availability (hosted/dedicated/private + region notes)
- provenance (template_bundle_version, generator_core_version, metadata_schema_hash)

Note: Even if “links” is a list conceptually, in storage we can keep JSON; but for this doc we just need to agree on fields. (Implementation detail: storage can be JSONB.)

---

11) Event producer considerations

11.1 Where should diff be computed?
Option 1: Producer computes diff
- Pros: generator simpler
- Cons: each producer must implement consistent diff logic

Option 2: Generator computes diff (preferred)
- Producer emits before_ref and after_ref (metadata snapshot IDs) or includes both payloads
- Pros: centralized diff semantics; consistent categories
- Cons: generator must be able to fetch snapshots reliably

MVP suggestion:
- For metadata_changed: include before/after snapshots (or references). We already have migration work; easiest is to include minimal diff summary fields in event payload while we build snapshot fetch.

11.2 Actor attribution
We need “who changed what” for audit. Producer must include actor:
- human_id if via admin console
- service name if automation
- request_id/trace_id

---

12) RBAC and security
- Public endpoints should only expose public entries.
- Internal endpoints require admin/support roles.
- Console UI incident showed internal notes leaking; generator should reduce the blast radius by never emitting internal fields in public artifacts.
- Audit logs: generator should emit audit log events on:
  - entry_published
  - entry_superseded
  - redaction_violation_detected (internal)

Open question (Marcus/Naomi): Should we treat “public release note published” as an auditable enterprise control event? Probably yes for Private.

---

13) Reliability / failure modes

Failure modes:
- Event bus outage: lag; Console shows stale notes (acceptable up to X hours?)
- Template rendering bug: could block publishing; must fail closed (do not publish partial) and alert
- Redaction false negatives: worst case; must be minimized via tests + CI preview
- Redaction false positives: blocks; needs override path (manual approval)

Suggested operational posture:
- Ingestion is at-least-once; store offsets and lag metrics.
- If rendering fails, store event in DLQ with reason; alert #eng-releases.
- Provide a “re-render” admin tool that creates a new entry_version (never overwrites published public entry).

---

14) Testing plan (early)
- Golden tests for templates: given fixed event+metadata fixture -> exact output markdown
- Redaction tests: ensure internal-only strings never appear in public output
- Replay tests: ingest same event 10x -> exactly 1 entry
- E2E: metadata edit -> CI preview -> promotion -> entry appears in Console feed and docs artifact

Leila: we should add an E2E scenario for rollback (version demoted / rollback promotion) once event type is finalized.

---

15) Open questions / TODOs
1) Event retention window: do we have 90 days of events to replay? (Logan to confirm.)
2) Account-scoped availability: do we need to model “enterprise canary account sees it first”? If yes, we must be careful with customer-visible history.
3) Template ownership: who approves template changes? (Probably Connor + Wei + PM.)
4) Do we need i18n? Likely no for v1.
5) How do we represent “quality change” without overclaiming? Need guardrail: only say “improved” if eval tag indicates significance (Jonas/Sana).
6) Private export: is the artifact embedded into upgrade bundle, or referenced? (Kira to advise.)

---

16) Next steps (proposed)
- Align on Option C (hybrid) with Dylan/Jada/Connor.
- Write the minimal rendered-entry schema and get buy-in from Console + docs.
- Implement generator-core package with:
  - diff categorization
  - template bundle v1
  - redaction engine
- Bring up changelog-generator service skeleton:
  - event ingestion
  - Postgres persistence
  - internal query APIs for Console
- Implement artifact export job for docs build.
- Plan backfill job (event replay + snapshot diff fallback).

Notes to self:
- Keep v1 small. We can add fancy rollouts-aware notes later (e.g., “available to 10% of Hosted traffic”). For now, stable release notes on promotion/deprecation are the win.
